candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record explicitly localizes the pregnancy to the anterior isthmic myometrium at the cesarean scar site, with a sac traversing the full width of the anterior myometrium and extending exophytically toward the serosa — hallmark imaging features of a cesarean scar ectopic pregnancy. An abdominal ectopic pregnancy implants in the peritoneal cavity outside the uterus, which is anatomically incompatible with the described findings. The two subtypes carry different management implications and are not interchangeable.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Abdominal ectopic vs. cesarean scar ectopic — both are ectopic pregnancies but anatomically distinct subtypes

case_quality_flags: Classic cesarean scar ectopic presentation with prior CS history, anterior isthmic sac, exophytic myometrial extension, and Doppler trophoblastic flow; diagnosis well-supported by imaging and operative findings
